NW Rare Game Empowerment project

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Nearly a billion rands worth of rare game from North West Parks is being donated in a transformation project - who are the beneficiaries who must feel that they won the lotto?

Summary:
At a launch on the farm, die Eiland in Swartruggens belonging to Mike de Kock of construction company Mcivils, based in Rustenburg, a game transformation project was launched for the North West on the 14th of August. The MEC, Manketsi Thlape was there giving the project her blessing as was Premier Supra Mahumapelo. On the surface the idea of using rare game to help black emerging game farmers to get into the business seems commendable, like a good idea. But dig a little deeper and it seems this is nothing more than a politically linked cabal stripping North west parks of valuable game.

The plan is to take 130 buffalo, 50 white rhino, 50 sable and 32 nyala from the parks. That effectively means there will be no nyala left as last years census shows a mere 27 in the parks. There are also only 99 sable so that will effectively leave a breeding population of 49, only half of which will be of breeding age. That's a very small gene pool and breeding population. Similarly when it comes to the buffalo there may be 1300 but 1000 of those are in Madikwe where they suffer from TB and another 50 in Mafikeng where they suffer from Bucellosis. So take 130 and you leave a population of only a 100 odd disease free buffalo, effrectively 50 breeding animals. And yet the project claims to be taking excess animals?

Further information:
So while there are serious conservation concerns there are other holes that can be poked in the project. SA rare game breeders association is run by Mike De Kock. He's new to the game, he doesn't have years and years of experience like other game farmers in the province. But what he does have is political connections within the province. He runs a civils company on Rustenburg that since 2009 has scored 1,9 billion rands worth of tenders. Most of these from the Rustenburg municipality. There's link number 2. Andries Boshoff is one of the co-directors of SARGBH. He happens to be the former mayor of Rustenburg who most recently worked as an administrator in the provincial legislature. Then comes another shock - one of the 5 selected beneficiaries is one Matthew Wolmarans - the former mayor of Rustenburg. He's a controversial figure. In 2011 he was arrested and jailed, along with his bodyguard for 20 years for the murder of councillor Moss Phakoe. The motive was that Phakoe had handed over a dossier of corruption to late minister of co-operative governance Sicelo Shiceka in his presence. Wolmarans confessed to the murder in jail according to reports but later recanted and appealed his murder conviction. He was released in 2013 having served 2 years after his lawyers poked holes in the case and questioned the credibility of key witnesses.

He now stands to make millions from the project along with 4 other beneficiaries selected by the MEC. We checked their addresses and despite claims that these were emerging working farmers 2 of the beneficiaries addresses are for low cost flats in townships in Mafikeng, bringing the emerging farmer argument into question. Andries Boshoff has admitted when I asked him at the launch if these were all established farmers that this was not the case. Wolmarans in another case in point.

So in the final analysis this is a money making scheme dreamt up by De Kock and his cronies, dressed up as a transformation project, but one that is set to benefit a group of politically connected individuals. It's completely out of kilter with conservation principles and I believe the audience and the public will be outraged by the scheme.

Press Release:


Public Game Private Profits
Our State nature reserves should be custodians of South African wildlife, conserving this natural heritage for all. So, why have millions of rands worth of taxpayer-owned game been donated to a group of businessmen and so-called emerging farmers by the North West provincial government, threatening the viability of remaining herds? This empowerment project could bring in billions of rands. Carte Blanche asks – who stands to benefit?


Script:


Script
Public Game, Private Money


VO: 31”
This rare group of buffalo is worth millions. They used to belong to the taxpayer as assets of north west parks. Now a provincial department has donated these animals along with 250 other rare game animals to an empowerment project. A group of wealthy businessmen and emerging black farmers are set to run the project. Andries Boshoff is the project leader. We met him on a farm where the animals will be bred over the next 10 years.

Andries:
This idea originated from South African rare game breeders, its an association of five game farmers who came together and we devised a strategy to approach government to say, how can we contribute to conservation and transformation of the wildlife industry.

VO: 6”
This is MEC Manketsi Tlhape from the department of Rural environment and agriculture development– she donated the animals for the project.

MEC:
As emerging, it means somebody needs to take them by hand, they need mentors and that is why we found it very appropriate that we should find people who could incubate them for a period of three years, that they can stand on their own and say we have the knowledge, we have the necessary skill.

VO: 15”
This is Mike de Kock – the project was his idea along with Andries Boshoff. SA rare game breeders will have a 50% shareholding, 5 black emerging farmers will have 40% and a farm workers trust will hold the remaining 10%. They’ll make their money by selling the offspring of the donated animals and then split the profits.

Derek:
So you personally will make money out of this project?

Andries:
I think so Derek, not in the short term, Derek, it’s a breeding programme its not an ATM. So you have to have a lot of commitment and passion for conservation and the wildlife industry to make money out of this.

Derek link
It’s claimed that the project is only taking excess animals from the parks but some experts say that it will impact on the breeding potential of the remaining herds.

VO:
The animals worth hundreds of millions of rands include 130 buffalo, 50 sable, 50 white rhino and 32 nyala. That works out to half the sable and disease free buffalo and the entire nyala population of north west parks.

Andries:
We are taking 262 animals in total, from the different parks. Animals that has been identified in terms of the habitat suitability study.

Derek:
Do you agree with those numbers? You’re taking virtually all the nyala population?

Andries:
In a specific park yes, not the population of the province. No.

Derek:
But you are decimating the herds?

Andries:
No, not at all.

VO:
That’s not true leaked census documents for 2014 show there is only one nyala herd and they are taking all of them. Jacqueline Theologo who serves on the legislature portfolio committee is worried.

Jacqueline:
What will be left in our parks for tourists to see and generations to come if they take all the top species then nothing will be left.

VO: 16”
This leaked memorandum drafted by the chief ecologist for North West – Piet Nel warns:

“Removing the numbers from the parks as proposed will seriously impact the viability and breeding potential of the remaining populations.”

MEC:
That I will not be able to say yes or no because that is an opinion. If a top ecologist like you say is saying that then that is an opinion, that he will still have to prove. And he can’t do that unless research is done.

Derek:
Why wasn’t the research done before the project?

MEC:
How do you do research if you don’t start something?

VO:
Ecologist Piet Nel could not be reached for comment but this north west parks insider is in agreement.

Insider:
The animals left behind is mostly skewed towards males, you’re taking basically the prime animals away because you want to breed so it is adult females or close to adult females, more females than males in any way.

VO: 4”
He says not everyone in north west parks supports this project.

Insider:
I think there is also some guys who are negative in relation towards this and I think some of them did give their opinions as well but we were over ruled.

VO:
Yet the MEC says she conducted due diligence.

MEC:
We have done our part as a province, as a provincial department. That is why we launched it daylight, media here and there and we were not even hiding it. That was why it was pronounced nationally during the state of the province address.


VO: 19”
But it seems the due diligence didn’t extend to the political animals involved. Andries it turns out has worked for the north west provincial legislature and is the former municipal manager of Rustenburg. His partner in the scheme, Mike De Kock, seen here at the project launch signing with the MEC has according to his own website, over a billion rands worth of tenders from Rustenburg municipality. In an email to us Mike nominated Andries to speak on his behalf.

Derek:
How are we meant to believe that this is an empowerment project rather than a money making scheme?

Andries:
Rustenburg local municipality did not do the game donation. It was done by North West Parks board. Mr Mike de Kock has got no connection in the North West parks board nor do I.


VO: 4”
There are also some question marks around the emerging farmers.

Derek:
Are you convinced they are all emerging farmers?

Andries:
They’ve been identified as emerging black farmers yes.

Derek:
Are you convinced of that?

Andries:
I am convinced yes.

VO: 6”
We did some research and found the closest any of the beneficiaries came was that one owned a cattle feedlot.

Derek:
Amongst the beneficiaries you’ve got the owners of a computer store, a musician, the owner of a transportation business. Where are the signs of emerging farmers here?

Andries:
Ja the interests of emerging farmers, they could have a variety of interests. We did not screen them. We did not select them.

Derek:
You were handed them by provincial government?

Andries:
Correct.

VO: 6”
Isaac Makwela, the only beneficiary allowed to speak to us – is also a former government employee,

Isaac:
I worked for the Department of Trade and industry in 2005, 2006 but before that I worked for the Department of Agriculture - national.


VO: 20”
He says showing an interest and attending government wildlife forums secured him his place in the scheme.
But we wondered how former Rustenburg mayor Matthew Wolmarans got his share. He was found guilty of the murder fellow councilor Moss Phakoe who wanted to expose corruption in the municipality. Wolmarans served 2 years of his 20 year sentence after being acquitted on appeal when his lawyers questioned the credibility of some of the witnesses in the case.

Derek:
Well it seems everybody is connected with the government here?

Andries:
Ja true, mister former mayor, Mr Wolmarans was also introduced to us as one of the beneficiaries. That’s correct.

Derek:
So how can he be an emerging farmer?

Andries:
Why not? Our deputy president is an astute game farmer. There’s nothing preventing Mr Wolmarans from becoming an emerging black farmer. He’s not involved in politics anymore.

MEC:
Now we cannot exclude people on what they ever did in the era that they did when they were mayors.

VO:
Andries says they had nothing to do with the choice of the beneficiaries..

Andries:
They were introduced to us at our inception meeting, that’s the first time that we met these individuals.

Derek:
Now you say you were introduced to the beneficiaries but you knew Matthew Wolmarans, you’d worked with him?

Andries:
Correct. At the first inception meeting, Mr Wolmarans with the four other beneficiaries were introduced to us. So that’s one of the beneficiaries that I knew prior this project. Because I used to work with him at the Rustenburg municipality.

Derek:
You don’t think a lot of people are going to look at this as just a little cabal to make money?

Andries:
I don’t think so Derek. If you look at the compliance regulations we had to go through, what we needed to submit to the North West Parks board, making sure that the grant is given, I’m sure that we did a lot of good work.

VO: 13”
These linkages may explain why the beneficiaries were never introduced at the recent project launch. Jacqueline challenged Premier Supra Mahumapelo on stage.

Jacqueline:
Sure behold I am going to look, I’m going to ask questions. I am going to scratch….
VO: 4”
She says there’s been a lack of transparency.

Derek:
What are your thoughts on the selection of the emerging farmers?

Jacqueline:
We don’t know how they got the names, how did they apply to get your name on the list. How was it advertised?

VO: 5”
And Andries it seemed wasn’t always forthcoming with the truth.

Derek:
Are you members of Wildlife ranching SA?

Andries:
Ja.

Derek: Because they say they don’t know who you are and how you got to run the project.

Andries:
You must just remember Derek South African rare game breeders holdings was just established. It’s a newly established pty limited, so that enrollment will still need to take place.

VO: 6”
After 10 years the project will return half of the original number of animals donated. We calculated earnings on the buffalos. Conservatively each buffalo is worth R700 thousand. Based on 100 cows over 10 years each producing one calf per year it’s estimated the beneficiaries could earn over a billion rand from buffalo alone.

Insider:
I believe the animals belong to the taxpayer because we are working with government money so not to a specific group of people.

Jacqueline:
To me it seems like a get rich quick scheme rather than looking after the animals.

VO:
But the MEC defends her decision.

Derek:
MEC do you think its ethical that the province’s rarest and finest game is used for private profit?

MEC:
It is also about expansion of conservation its not for profit only. We are looking at economic development, economic empowerment yes but also as a province our main objective is accede to the national call that conservation areas, protected areas need to be expanded.

VO:
But none of these profits will go back into north west parks’ own conservation fund. As they say, the devil here is in the detail.


Promo 1: 10 sec

Our state game parks are meant to be custodians of our wildlife – they are meant to conserve our natural heritage. We ask why are connected individuals standing to profit?


Promo 2: 15 sec

VO: 10”
The controversial mayor, the former municipal manager and the businesman with over a billion rands worth of tenders from Rustenburg municipality. Why are they benefitting from provincial rare game?

Andries: not an ATM


Promo 3: 15 sec

VO: 9”
A rare game empowerment project in the north west province is threatening the viability of the remaining herds.

Insider: mostly skewed towards males….because you want to breed.

His partner in the scheme, Mike De Kock, seen here at the project launch signing with the MEC has according to his own website, over a billion rands worth of tenders from Rustenburg municipality. In an email to us Mike nominated Andries to speak on his behalf. Derek: How are we meant to believe that this is an empowerment project rather than a money making scheme? Andries: Rustenburg local municipality did not do the game donation. It was done by North West Parks board. Mr Mike de Kock has got no connection in the North West parks board nor do I. VO: 4” There are also some question marks around the emerging farmers. Derek: Are you convinced they are all emerging farmers? Andries: They’ve been identified as emerging black farmers yes. Derek: Are you convinced of that? Andries: I am convinced yes. VO: 6” We did some research and found the closest any of the beneficiaries came was that one owned a cattle feedlot. Derek: Amongst the beneficiaries you’ve got the owners of a computer store, a musician, the owner of a transportation business. Where are the signs of emerging farmers here? Andries: Ja the interests of emerging farmers, they could have a variety of interests. We did not screen them. We did not select them. Derek: You were handed them by provincial government? Andries: Correct. VO: 6” Isaac Makwela, the only beneficiary allowed to speak to us – is also a former government employee, Isaac: I worked for the Department of Trade and industry in 2005, 2006 but before that I worked for the Department of Agriculture - national. VO: 20” He says showing an interest and attending government wildlife forums secured him his place in the scheme. But we wondered how former Rustenburg mayor Matthew Wolmarans got his share. He was found guilty of the murder fellow councilor Moss Phakoe who wanted to expose corruption in the municipality. Wolmarans served 2 years of his 20 year sentence after being acquitted on appeal when his lawyers questioned the credibility of some of the witnesses in the case. Derek: Well it seems everybody is connected with the government here? Andries: Ja true, mister former mayor, Mr Wolmarans was also introduced to us as one of the beneficiaries. That’s correct. Derek: So how can he be an emerging farmer? Andries: Why not? Our deputy president is an astute game farmer. There’s nothing preventing Mr Wolmarans from becoming an emerging black farmer. He’s not involved in politics anymore. MEC: Now we cannot exclude people on what they ever did in the era that they did when they were mayors. VO: Andries says they had nothing to do with the choice of the beneficiaries.. Andries: They were introduced to us at our inception meeting, that’s the first time that we met these individuals. Derek: Now you say you were introduced to the beneficiaries but you knew Matthew Wolmarans, you’d worked with him? Andries: Correct. At the first inception meeting, Mr Wolmarans with the four other beneficiaries were introduced to us. So that’s one of the beneficiaries that I knew prior this project. Because I used to work with him at the Rustenburg municipality. Derek: You don’t think a lot of people are going to look at this as just a little cabal to make money? Andries: I don’t think so Derek. If you look at the compliance regulations we had to go through, what we needed to submit to the North West Parks board, making sure that the grant is given, I’m sure that we did a lot of good work. VO: 13” These linkages may explain why the beneficiaries were never introduced at the recent project launch. Jacqueline challenged Premier Supra Mahumapelo on stage. Jacqueline: Sure behold I am going to look, I’m going to ask questions. I am going to scratch…. VO: 4” She says there’s been a lack of transparency. Derek: What are your thoughts on the selection of the emerging farmers? Jacqueline: We don’t know how they got the names, how did they apply to get your name on the list. How was it advertised? VO: 5” And Andries it seemed wasn’t always forthcoming with the truth. Derek: Are you members of Wildlife ranching SA? Andries: Ja. Derek: Because they say they don’t know who you are and how you got to run the project. Andries: You must just remember Derek South African rare game breeders holdings was just established. It’s a newly established pty limited, so that enrollment will still need to take place. VO: 6” After 10 years the project will return half of the original number of animals donated. We calculated earnings on the buffalos. Conservatively each buffalo is worth R700 thousand. Based on 100 cows over 10 years each producing one calf per year it’s estimated the beneficiaries could earn over a billion rand from buffalo alone. Insider: I believe the animals belong to the taxpayer because we are working with government money so not to a specific group of people. Jacqueline: To me it seems like a get rich quick scheme rather than looking after the animals. VO: But the MEC defends her decision. Derek: MEC do you think its ethical that the province’s rarest and finest game is used for private profit? MEC: It is also about expansion of conservation its not for profit only. We are looking at economic development, economic empowerment yes but also as a province our main objective is accede to the national call that conservation areas, protected areas need to be expanded. VO: But none of these profits will go back into north west parks’ own conservation fund. As they say, the devil here is in the detail. Promo 1: 10 sec Our state game parks are meant to be custodians of our wildlife – they are meant to conserve our natural heritage. We ask why are connected individuals standing to profit? Promo 2: 15 sec VO: 10” The controversial mayor, the former municipal manager and the businesman with over a billion rands worth of tenders from Rustenburg municipality. Why are they benefitting from provincial rare game? Andries: not an ATM Promo 3: 15 sec VO: 9” A rare game empowerment project in the north west province is threatening the viability of the remaining herds. Insider: mostly skewed towards males….because you want to breed.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Nearly a billion rands worth of rare game from North West Parks is being donated in a transformation project - who are the beneficiaries who must feel that they won the lotto?
metadata.Summary: At a launch on the farm, die Eiland in Swartruggens belonging to Mike de Kock of construction company Mcivils, based in Rustenburg, a game transformation project was launched for the North West on the 14th of August. The MEC, Manketsi Thlape was there giving the project her blessing as was Premier Supra Mahumapelo. On the surface the idea of using rare game to help black emerging game farmers to get into the business seems commendable, like a good idea. But dig a little deeper and it seems this is nothing more than a politically linked cabal stripping North west parks of valuable game. The plan is to take 130 buffalo, 50 white rhino, 50 sable and 32 nyala from the parks. That effectively means there will be no nyala left as last years census shows a mere 27 in the parks. There are also only 99 sable so that will effectively leave a breeding population of 49, only half of which will be of breeding age. That's a very small gene pool and breeding population. Similarly when it comes to the buffalo there may be 1300 but 1000 of those are in Madikwe where they suffer from TB and another 50 in Mafikeng where they suffer from Bucellosis. So take 130 and you leave a population of only a 100 odd disease free buffalo, effrectively 50 breeding animals. And yet the project claims to be taking excess animals?
metadata.Further information: So while there are serious conservation concerns there are other holes that can be poked in the project. SA rare game breeders association is run by Mike De Kock. He's new to the game, he doesn't have years and years of experience like other game farmers in the province. But what he does have is political connections within the province. He runs a civils company on Rustenburg that since 2009 has scored 1,9 billion rands worth of tenders. Most of these from the Rustenburg municipality. There's link number 2. Andries Boshoff is one of the co-directors of SARGBH. He happens to be the former mayor of Rustenburg who most recently worked as an administrator in the provincial legislature. Then comes another shock - one of the 5 selected beneficiaries is one Matthew Wolmarans - the former mayor of Rustenburg. He's a controversial figure. In 2011 he was arrested and jailed, along with his bodyguard for 20 years for the murder of councillor Moss Phakoe. The motive was that Phakoe had handed over a dossier of corruption to late minister of co-operative governance Sicelo Shiceka in his presence. Wolmarans confessed to the murder in jail according to reports but later recanted and appealed his murder conviction. He was released in 2013 having served 2 years after his lawyers poked holes in the case and questioned the credibility of key witnesses. He now stands to make millions from the project along with 4 other beneficiaries selected by the MEC. We checked their addresses and despite claims that these were emerging working farmers 2 of the beneficiaries addresses are for low cost flats in townships in Mafikeng, bringing the emerging farmer argument into question. Andries Boshoff has admitted when I asked him at the launch if these were all established farmers that this was not the case. Wolmarans in another case in point. So in the final analysis this is a money making scheme dreamt up by De Kock and his cronies, dressed up as a transformation project, but one that is set to benefit a group of politically connected individuals. It's completely out of kilter with conservation principles and I believe the audience and the public will be outraged by the scheme. Interviews: Mike De Kock - SA Rare Game Breeders Holdings Andries Boshoff former Municipal manager of Rustenburg and now part of SARGBH Matthew Wolmarans - former Rustenburg Mayor MEC Manketsi Thlape Jacqueline Theologo - portfolio committee opposed to the plan EWT - why should they use our wildlife in this way? NW parks insider - hidden ID I have cellphone footage of the launch, speeches by MEC, Premier and SARGBH as well as Mike and the MEC signing the project agreement.
